extra.reason: Decided: archive the repo and unlist the template (2026-08-05). This closes the open question — archiving freezes the release/commitlint/gallery workflows installed in PR #3, which is the accepted cost of ending the repo's life. master is left coherent at v1.0.1 with a README pointing at axeptio/axeptio-gtm-public-template. Reversible via 'gh repo unarchive' if ever needed.

Moot. Archiving makes GitHub issues read-only, so the stale bot cannot mark anything on this repo again. The one issue it mishandled (#1) was answered and closed on 2026-07-29, and the reply explicitly disowns the stale comment. If the same bot runs on other Axeptio repos the underlying concern still stands there — not tracked here.

Wontfix. Repo archived, so LICENSE is frozen with the unfilled 'Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]' appendix. The Apache 2.0 grant is valid regardless, and the template is unlisted, so the gallery constraint that made LICENSE load-bearing no longer applies.

Wontfix. Repo archived and template unlisted, so the gallery placeholders (cvt_temp_public_id, brand_dummy), the missing categories, the French TODO and the empty ___TESTS___ block are all frozen as-is. These only mattered for a resubmission, which is no longer on the table.

Closed only because this repo is being archived — the work itself is NOT done and does not belong to this repo. Re-file against axeptio/axeptio-gtm-public-template.

Its scripts/validate-gallery.py still has all three bugs fixed here in commit 9bbfed1:
1. git() raises FileNotFoundError when git is not on PATH — traceback instead of a clear failure. Fix: catch OSError, return None, and gate every check behind a check_git_available() preflight.
2. 'git ls-files' return code unchecked — an empty result reads as 'nothing is tracked' and emits a screenful of invented violations (including a misleading LICENSE-casing failure) instead of the one real problem.
3. template.tpl is never checked for being git-tracked, unlike LICENSE, so a locally-untracked template passes validation while it would not ship.

Separately, that repo's committed .beads/issues.jsonl publishes a personal email address (pleberre@icloud.com) in the owner field of every issue, on a PUBLIC repo. bd derives owner from git user.email and has no --owner flag, and auto-export clobbers hand-edits, so the fix is at the source: set a repo-local noreply user.email, then delete and recreate the issues. Same finding Copilot raised on PR #3 here.

Reference implementation: axeptio/GTM_consent_mode_template @ 9bbfed1 and b1b3171.
